verdict.rationale: The official docs state that ScrapingBee's headless browsers wait for a CSS or XPath selector passed as a parameter before returning the HTML. JavaScript rendering is on by default, and the JS scenario also offers a `wait_for_and_click` instruction. missing for 10: the parameter name and timeout/failure behaviour are not shown in the evidence, and there is no independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the API wait for a specific selector to appear before returning the rendered page

citations.quote: Our headless browsers will wait for the CSS / Xpath selector passed in the parameter before returning the HTML.
JavaScript rendering is enabled by default.
